frameworks.name: S&ME Investment Framework
frameworks.definition: Allocate 100% of excess income to education (courses, coaching, mentorships, workshops) that increases earning capacity rather than passive assets, because earning capacity compounds faster than 10% annual returns.

frameworks.name: Skills Stack Exponential Growth
frameworks.definition: Each additional skill multiplies return on existing skills: videography + editing + social media + copywriting + branding + operations + leadership creates a CMO-level asset that compounds earning capacity 10x faster than base skills alone.

frameworks.name: Bridge-Building Discipline
frameworks.definition: Completing one skill stack fully (all 30 bricks to first dollar) is superior to building many half-finished bridges; speed of mastery depends on identifying which brick is missing and focusing there.

claims.text: Investing $500 in a two-day phlebotomist certification that raises hourly wages from $7.50 to $25/hour triples earning capacity and produces 50+ years of higher income, making the $500 ROI decision trivially favorable at age 18.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: age 18 or early career with minimal skills
certification path available (phlebotomy, similar technical skills)
long remaining working lifespan
claims.mechanism: Skill certification directly increases hourly rate, which compounds over decades of deployment.
bounded_by: Assumes certification is readily available and legitimate
Does not apply if labor market is saturated or wages are legally capped

claims.text: A 20-year-old earning $50,000 annually after tax can live on $20,000 (roommates, ramen), leaving $25,000-$30,000 annually ($2,000/month) to invest entirely in education: courses, coaching, mentorships, workshops.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: age 20 with moderate earning capacity
ability to live communally (roommates available)
minimal family/dependent obligations
claims.mechanism: Living expenses are controllable; education spending is the highest-ROI capital allocation at this life stage.

numbers.axis: annual income and budget allocation by life stage

bounded_by: Does not apply in high cost-of-living regions where $20k cannot cover rent + food
Does not apply if family obligations or dependents exist

claims.text: Allocating $2,000 per month to education (courses, coaching, mentorships) for four years will produce earning capacity exceeding typical four-year degree holders by the end of year four, with initial income arriving within the first year.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: consistent allocation of $2,000/month over 4-year period
selection of high-quality education providers
active implementation of skills learned (not passive consumption)
age 20-24 (early career)
claims.mechanism: Targeted skill investment directly increases market value; breadth of applied skills (copywriting, media buying, operations, leadership) creates versatility that degree holders lack.
bounded_by: Does not guarantee outcomes without sustained implementation
Assumes education providers deliver quality instruction and mentorship

claims.text: Your earning capacity—the value of problems you solve and the price you charge—is the fundamental wealth-generation lever; this capacity compounds faster (10x+) than passive asset returns (S&P 500 at ~10% annually).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: age 20-35 (career-building years)
active skill deployment in market (not speculative investment)
claims.mechanism: Earned income from applied skills can double, triple, or 10x annually through iteration and market feedback; passive portfolio returns are fixed by market conditions.

numbers.axis: annual return rate on capital allocation

anchors.region: earning capacity improvement via applied skills

bounded_by: Earning capacity growth requires active market engagement; pure passive investment cannot match it
Market saturation, competitive barriers, and skill gaps can limit upside

claims.text: Real estate wealth-building is exclusively active-income work (deal sourcing, construction management, capital sourcing), not passive; claims of passive real estate wealth are misleading because the builder spent thousands of hours sourcing deals and managing contractors.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: real estate as primary wealth vehicle
comparing real estate to true passive investment strategies
claims.mechanism: Real estate wealth requires active decision-making and operational work; the hours spent are invisible in outcome-focused narratives, creating false perception of passivity.
bounded_by: Does not apply to REITs or true passive real estate investment vehicles
Some commercial properties with hired management approach semi-passive status

claims.text: One-on-one coaching or course purchases should be framed as individual bricks in an entrepreneurial degree, not as a single savior purchase; expecting one course to create wealth is a failure of expectation-setting, not the course's fault.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: purchasing courses, coaching, or educational products
goal of skill acquisition and earning capacity growth
claims.mechanism: Educational purchases compound when stacked sequentially; individual courses are isolated value without integration into a broader learning system.
bounded_by: Does not apply to prerequisite courses that unlock foundational knowledge
Meta-skills (learning itself) may have higher leverage than domain skills

claims.text: Following a teacher's content for free first (YouTube, Instagram, free resources) reduces purchase risk by allowing pre-purchase validation that their paid offering matches their free teaching quality.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: considering paid course or coaching purchase
teacher has published substantial free content
evaluation window of 7 days before purchase decision
claims.mechanism: Free content is a quality signal; if free work is poor, paid work is unlikely to be better; if free work is excellent, paid work has high probability of quality.
bounded_by: Does not apply if the teacher is entirely hidden (no free content available)
Free content quality does not guarantee paid product quality, only increases likelihood

claims.text: Purchasing courses from multiple teachers in the same field enables comparison and comprehensive mastery, increasing total knowledge beyond any single teacher.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: budget of $4,000+/month for education
specific domain with multiple quality teachers
goal of mastery vs. beginner competence
claims.mechanism: Cross-teacher comparison reveals blind spots, teaching style preferences, and domain gaps; synthesis of multiple perspectives creates superior mental models.
bounded_by: Does not improve outcomes if course purchases are scattered across unrelated domains
Diminishing returns after 3-5 courses on the same topic due to redundancy

claims.text: Replication before iteration: master the exact method of a teacher (copy the bricks) before adding personal variations; earning the right to iterate requires first proving you can duplicate.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: learning from an established teacher or framework
skill where proven systems exist (sales, marketing, operations)
claims.mechanism: Copying prevents idiosyncratic mistakes; once replication produces results, iteration can be informed by success, not guesswork.
bounded_by: Does not apply to creative fields where style differentiation is primary value
Assumes the teacher's method is generalizable to your context

claims.text: Skill stacking creates exponential earning growth: a videographer who learns editing, messaging, copywriting, branding, operations, and leadership becomes a CMO-level operator earning 10x initial rate.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: starting with foundational skill (videography, copywriting, sales, etc.)
sequential addition of complementary skills
integration of skills into cohesive offering
claims.mechanism: Each skill multiplies value of existing skills; breadth creates leveraged position unavailable to single-skill specialists.

numbers.axis: earning multiplier based on skill count

anchors.region: 5-7 integrated skills (editing + messaging + copywriting + branding + operations + leadership)

bounded_by: Does not apply if skills are unrelated (deep expertise in unrelated silos)
Integration and positioning are required; isolated skills don't compound

claims.text: Personal capital allocation rule at age 20-30: spend 0% on passive asset investment (S&P, real estate), allocate 100% of excess income to education increasing earning capacity because it compounds faster.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: age 20-30 with minimal assets
active income stream already established
goal of maximum wealth accumulation
claims.mechanism: Earning capacity growth via education yields 10-100x returns annually; asset investment yields 10% annually; opportunity cost of asset investment during peak earning-capacity years is extreme.
bounded_by: Does not apply if you already have sufficient emergency reserves ($10k-$25k)
Does not apply once earning capacity reaches $100k+/year (diminishing returns on education spend)
Assumes you have consistent income to live on while investing all excess

claims.text: The richest people earn thousands to millions of times more per hour than average workers; Jeff Bezos earned $40 million per hour last year, illustrating that earning capacity is the true wealth lever.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: extreme wealth comparison across earning stages
measurement of hourly earning capacity
claims.mechanism: Higher earning capacity per hour is achieved through business models, leverage, and market position, not asset accumulation alone.
bounded_by: Billionaire earnings are not sustainable by typical operators
Hourly rate calculation assumes active ownership; passive dividend income differs

examples.text: At Brooke's house, a 20-23 year old had $1,000 extra and asked where to invest it. He mentioned he already had a 401k and other investments. This represents the common thinking of young earners who see passive investment as the default, not recognizing that earning capacity investment at age 20 yields orders of magnitude higher returns.

A videographer learns editing, then social media and messaging, then copywriting and branding, then management, operations, and leadership. By integrating these skills, they transition from a $50/hour videographer to a $500+/hour CMO-level operator. The compounding is exponential because each new skill magnifies the value of existing skills.

Real estate investors claim they made $X on a single deal, but they omit the thousands of hours spent sourcing deals, walking buildings, interviewing contractors, and managing general contractors. They frame it as passive wealth but the process is exclusively active work.

practices.text: At age 20, live as cheap as possible (roommates, minimal lifestyle) to maximize the gap between income and expenses.
Allocate 100% of excess income (after living expenses) to education that increases earning capacity: courses, coaching, mentorships, workshops, seminars.
Spend $2,000 per month on educational purchases rather than investing in S&P, real estate, or passive vehicles.
Follow potential teachers' free content (Instagram, YouTube) for 7 days before purchasing their paid courses to validate quality.
When purchasing courses, approach each as a single brick in your entrepreneurial degree, not as a standalone savior.
Buy courses from multiple teachers in the same field to synthesize comprehensive knowledge rather than relying on a single source.
Replicate a proven method exactly before iterating on it; copy the bricks first, then earn the right to modify.
Identify which skill brick is missing from your bridge and focus your learning attention there to accelerate progress.
